name: Introduction to Mobile Robotics
description:
(I) Foundations:
  Introduction
  Mathematical Foundations
  Locomotion
  Sensors for Mobile Robots

(II) Probabilistic Robot State Estimation
  Recursive Bayes Filtering
  Probabilistic Sensor Models
  Probabilistic Motion Models
  Discrete Bayes Filters
  Gaussian Representation (Kalman Filter)
  Extended Kalman Filter
  Particle Filter

(III)Probabilistic Environment State Estimation with known poses
  Occupancy Grid Maps
  Reflection Maps

(IV) SLAM
  EKF-SLAM
  FastSLAM 
  Graph-SLAM

(V) Path-Planning and Collision Avoidance
  Collision Avoidance
  Path Planning

(VI) Exploration
  Multi-robot Exploration
  Information-theoretic Exploration
prerequisites:
Fundamental mathematical knowledge is expected. Though the most relevant mathematical concepts are introduced within the course, the students are expected to have experience with linear algebra, probability theory, and mathematical analysis.

Further, we expect Python programming skills for the homework classes.

Additionally, we recommend participation in the following courses:
- Computer Vision II: Multi-View Geometry (IN2228), 
- Robotics (IN2067), 
- Robot Motion Planning (IN2138), 
- Motion planning for autonomous vehicles (IN2106, IN0012, IN4221)
- Mobile Robotics (IN2404)
